html:
The Kirghiz Soviet Socialist Republic was the Kyrgyz republic of the Soviet Union, a full union republic from 5 December 1936 until it declared independence on 31 August 1991.

Soviet planners first drew a Kyrgyz unit in the division of Central Asia in 1924, giving the herders of the Tian Shan a territory of their own for the first time. Collectivisation forced the nomads onto farms, and many died or fled to China. Schools spread literacy, in Kyrgyz and Russian, and writers such as Chinghiz Aitmatov became famous across the Union.

The borders cut across the Fergana valley, leaving many Uzbeks in Kyrgyzstan and Kyrgyz in Uzbekistan, a cause of later clashes. When the Soviet Union broke up, the physicist Askar Akayev became the first president of independent Kyrgyzstan.
sum: The Kirghiz Soviet Socialist Republic was the Kyrgyz republic of the Soviet Union, a full union republic from 5 December 1936 until it declared independence on 31 August 1991.
